title: A Student's Daily Routine
lines: My name is Daniel, and I'm a student.
Today, I'm going to tell you about my daily routine.
On weekdays, I usually wake up at seven o'clock.
I don't like getting up early, especially when the weather is cold, but I have to get ready for school.
First, I wash my face and brush my teeth.
Then I get dressed and go to the kitchen.
My mother usually prepares breakfast for the family.
I normally have eggs, bread, and tea.
Sometimes I eat cereal with milk if I don't have much time.
I leave home at about half past seven.
My school is not very far away, so I usually walk there.
I like walking because I can get some fresh air before my lessons start.
If it rains, my father sometimes drives me to school.
I study different subjects, including English, mathematics, history, and science.
English is my favourite subject because I enjoy learning new words and speaking with my classmates.
Mathematics is a little more difficult for me, but I try to practise it every day.
We have a short break at ten thirty.
I usually talk to my friends or buy something small to eat.
Our lunch break is at twelve thirty.
I often bring a sandwich and some fruit from home, but sometimes I eat lunch in the school cafeteria.
When I get home, I have lunch if I'm hungry and then take a short rest.
After that, I do my homework.
I usually spend about one hour on it, but some days I need more time.
In the evening, I like listening to music, watching videos, or playing computer games.
I also help my parents with small jobs around the house.
For example, I sometimes wash the dishes or tidy my room.
We usually have dinner together at seven thirty.
After dinner, I prepare my school bag and choose my clothes for the next day.
I don't want to do these things in the morning because I'm often in a hurry.
Before going to bed, I sometimes read a few pages of a book.
I usually go to bed at ten thirty.
I know that getting enough sleep is important, so I try not to stay up late.
My weekends are quite different because I don't have to go to school.

title: A Family Conversation
lines: I spent most of it with my family.
We had a small family lunch on Sunday.
How many people are there in your family?
There are five of us: my parents, my older sister, my younger brother, and me.
My grandparents live in another town, but they visit us quite often.
Do you get along well with your brother and sister?
My sister is twenty, so she's older than me by three years.
She's quite responsible and always helps me with my studies.
My younger brother is only eight.
He's funny and energetic, but sometimes he makes a lot of noise.
I have a younger sister too.
She's ten, and we share a bedroom.
Sometimes we argue because she takes my things without asking.
My brother sometimes uses my headphones.
I tell him to ask me first, but he forgets.
He works in an office and usually comes home at six.
She works at a primary school not far from our house.
Does your mother help you with your homework?
But my sister is better at mathematics, so I usually ask her for help with that subject.
What do you usually do together as a family?
At weekends, we sometimes watch a film or visit my grandparents.
My father also enjoys cooking, so he prepares special meals on Sundays.
What did you do at your family lunch yesterday?
My grandmother made her famous chicken soup, and my father prepared a big dish of plov.
We also had a salad and some fruit.
After lunch, we sat in the garden and talked.
I don't see my grandparents very often because they live far away.
You should call them more often.
My grandmother really enjoys talking on the phone.
She always asks me about school and my friends.
Family is important, even when everyone is busy.

title: Finding a New House
lines: I'm looking for a house to rent.
My family and I want to move next month.
How many bedrooms do you need?
We have two children, and they need their own space.
We would also like a small garden.
Do you have a monthly budget?
We'd prefer to pay around eight hundred dollars a month.
We could pay a little more for the right house, but we don't want anything too expensive.
The first one is in the city centre.
It has three bedrooms, a large kitchen, and a comfortable living room.
There is a supermarket across the street, and the bus stop is only two minutes away.
It has a small balcony instead.
The rent is seven hundred and fifty dollars per month.
We really want a garden because our children enjoy playing outside.
The second house is in a quieter neighbourhood, about twenty minutes from the city centre by bus.
It has three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and a lovely garden.
There is also a small park nearby.
Is there a supermarket in the area?
There is one about five minutes away on foot.
There is also a primary school near the park.
Eight hundred and twenty dollars per month.
Water and heating are included, but electricity is not.
That's a little above our budget, but it might be possible.
It has a sofa, a dining table, and some kitchen cupboards.
However, there are no beds or wardrobes.
Can we visit the house this week?
I have an appointment available on Thursday at four in the afternoon.
Thursday at four works for me.
Could I have your phone number so I can confirm the appointment?
I'll give it to you now.

title: Food Around the World
lines: Today, we're going to talk about food around the world.
Food is an important part of every culture.
People in different countries eat different meals, use different ingredients, and have their own cooking traditions.
Italian food is famous in many countries.
Pizza and pasta are two of the most popular dishes.
Italian people often use tomatoes, cheese, olive oil, and fresh vegetables.
Many families enjoy eating together, especially at weekends.
A traditional Italian meal can take quite a long time because people like talking while they eat.
Rice is an important part of Japanese food.
Many people eat rice with fish, vegetables, and soup.
Sushi is one of the most famous Japanese dishes.
It usually contains rice and fish, although there are different types.
Japanese meals are often simple and carefully prepared.
In Mexico, food is usually full of flavour.
People put meat, vegetables, cheese, or beans inside small tortillas.
Some Mexican dishes are spicy because cooks use different kinds of peppers.
However, not every Mexican meal is hot.
There are also many sweet dishes and desserts.
Indian food is known for its spices.
People use ingredients such as rice, potatoes, tomatoes, and different spices.
Curry is a popular dish, and there are many different versions.
Some people eat meat, while others prefer vegetarian meals.
In fact, vegetarian food is very common in many parts of India.
Uzbek cuisine has a long history and many traditional dishes.
Plov is probably the most famous one.
It is usually made with rice, meat, carrots, onions, and oil.
People often prepare it for family celebrations and special events.
Other popular dishes include somsa, manti, and shashlik.
Although food is different around the world, it brings people together.
Families share meals, friends meet at restaurants, and people celebrate important moments with special dishes.
So, next time you try food from another country, remember that you are also learning something about its culture.

title: Weekend Plans
lines: My cousin is visiting us this weekend.
I want to show her around the city, but I don't know where to take her.
She's seventeen, and she's really interested in photography.
She loves taking pictures of interesting buildings and beautiful places.
Then you should take her to the old part of the city.
There are some beautiful historical buildings there.
The streets are quite narrow, but they look amazing in photographs.
Is there anything else we can do?
Well, there's a new art exhibition at the city museum.
My sister went there yesterday, and she said it was really interesting.
No, the tickets are quite cheap.
I think they're around five dollars for students.
I don't want to spend the whole day walking around without eating anything.
There's a small Italian restaurant near the museum.
I went there with my family last month.
The food was delicious, and the prices were reasonable.
Yes, they have several vegetarian dishes.
My sister ordered a vegetable pizza, and she really enjoyed it.
Maybe we can invite some other friends too.
They usually have free time on Saturdays.
I'll send them a message tonight.
By the way, what time should we meet?
How about nine thirty in the morning?
We can meet in front of the central library.
I usually wake up at nine on Saturdays!
We have a lot to see.
But we can make it ten o'clock if you prefer.
I'll probably take a taxi because the bus is always crowded in the morning.
I think I'll come by bicycle.
The weather forecast says it will be sunny, so it should be a pleasant ride.
I'll bring my camera, and Sophie can use my old phone to take pictures too.
Don't forget to charge your camera tonight.

title: Two Friends Talking
lines: I haven't seen you for a few days.
I've started going to a new sports club.
What kind of sport do you do there?
I play basketball three times a week.
I've always liked basketball, but I never had enough time to practise regularly.
Do you play with your school friends?
But the club has different groups.
My group has twelve people, and most of them are around my age.
Our coach is very friendly, but he expects us to work hard.
How long are your training sessions?
We usually start with some simple exercises to warm up.
Then we practise passing, shooting, and working as a team.
At the end, we play a short match.
I used to play basketball when I was younger, but I stopped because I didn't have a good team.
We need one more player for our Saturday group.
I'd love to, but I'm not very good at basketball anymore.
Nobody expects you to be perfect.
The important thing is to practise and enjoy the game.
How much does the club cost?
You can also pay for three months together, which is a little cheaper.
Do I need to bring anything?
Just sports clothes, comfortable trainers, and a bottle of water.
They have basketballs at the club, so you don't need to buy one.
It's next to the city swimming pool, about ten minutes from the central bus station.
You can take bus number six.
It stops right outside the sports centre.
What time do you train on Saturdays?
Our session starts at eleven in the morning.
But I usually arrive fifteen minutes early because I like to get ready before training.
I think I'll come with you this Saturday.
You can watch the first half, and then you can join us if you want.
By the way, do you do any other activities?
I also go swimming on Sundays.
It's a good way to relax after a busy week.
I used to spend most of my weekends playing computer games, but now I prefer doing something active.
I should probably do the same.
I spend too much time sitting at home.
You don't have to change everything at once.
Just start with one activity you enjoy.
I'll see you on Saturday, then.
And don't forget your water bottle!

title: A School Announcement
lines: I have some important information about activities at our school next week.
Please listen carefully and write down anything you need to remember.
First, let's talk about the school library.
From Monday, the library will open at eight thirty in the morning instead of nine.
It will close at four thirty in the afternoon.
Students can borrow up to three books at a time.
You can keep each book for two weeks.
If you need more time, you can ask the librarian to extend the borrowing period.
Next, we are organising a school sports day on Wednesday.
It will take place on the school playground, starting at ten o'clock.
There will be several activities, including football, basketball, volleyball, and running competitions.
Students who want to take part should give their names to their class teachers before Tuesday afternoon.
Remember to wear comfortable sports clothes and bring a bottle of water.
Now, some information about the English club.
We have decided to change the meeting day.
The club usually meets on Thursday, but next week it will meet on Friday at three fifteen.
The meeting will be in Room 12, not Room 8.
We will watch a short film and discuss the characters and the story.
You don't need to prepare anything before the meeting.
There is also a science exhibition in the main hall next Thursday.
Students from different classes have prepared small projects about animals, plants, and the environment.
The exhibition will open at nine in the morning and finish at one o'clock.
You can visit it with your classmates during your free lesson.
Please remember that food and drinks are not allowed in the exhibition area.
Finally, I want to remind everyone about the school trip.
We are going to the history museum on Friday, the twenty-first of this month.
The bus will leave from the school entrance at eight fifteen, so please arrive at least fifteen minutes early.
The journey will take about forty minutes.
You should bring a packed lunch, a notebook, and a pen.
The school will pay for the bus, but students need to bring money for their museum tickets.
If you have any questions about these activities, please speak to your class teacher.
Thank you for listening, and have a good day!

title: An Interview About Hobbies
lines: Welcome to Teen Life, the show for young people with big ideas.
Today we're talking about hobbies, and our guest is a student from our city, Olivia Green.
Olivia, could you spell your surname for our listeners?
Thank you. And thank you for coming in so early in the morning!
I know most teenagers are still in bed at this time.
So, let's start with the big question: what do you enjoy doing in your free time?
Well, I'm not a big fan of early mornings, but this was worth it.
At first I took photos with my mum's phone, but the pictures weren't very good, and she always wanted her phone back!
My dad wanted to buy me a camera for my birthday, but new cameras are really expensive.
Then my uncle gave me his old camera.
It's quite heavy, but it takes beautiful pictures.
He's a photographer, so he taught me a lot.
I like taking pictures of nature.
I've tried taking photos of people too, but my little sister always pulls funny faces!
So now I mostly photograph birds and flowers.
Lovely. I'm sure our listeners would like to see them one day!
Where do you take your photos?
Usually in a park near my house.
It's very close, so I can walk there with my camera.
It has a big lake and lots of tall trees, and in spring there are ducks with their babies everywhere.
You need to be patient, though.
Sometimes I wait for half an hour to get one good picture!
I usually go there on Saturday mornings.
I take a flask of hot chocolate, sit on a bench by the lake, and just wait.
My uncle says the light is better in the morning, but that's not the reason.
I go then because it's quiet, and there aren't many people to scare the birds.
Yes, I love baking with my grandmother.
She lives next door, so I visit her a lot.
We usually make biscuits, because they're quick and my grandfather eats them all!
Her biscuits are famous in our street.
Everyone asks her for the recipe, but she never tells them!
She never uses a website or a cookbook.
Instead, she has an old notebook full of family recipes, and we try a new one every week.
Some of the recipes are a hundred years old!
The writing is very small, so sometimes I read them out loud for her.
And I'm getting better at baking on my own, too.
Last month, I made a chocolate cake for my best friend's birthday.
She cried a little when she saw it, and then we ate the whole cake in ten minutes.
Photography and baking! How do you find time for all this?
During the week, I do my homework first, because my parents are very strict about that.
Then I have some free time in the evening, but only an hour or so.
At weekends, I have much more time for my hobbies.
My friends sometimes say I'm too busy, but I'm happy!
Do you have a goal for this year?
Yes! I'd like to enter a photography competition.
I saw a poster for it at school last week.
It's for teenagers aged thirteen to seventeen, and you can send up to five photos.
I've already chosen three: a big white bird by the lake, a red flower after the rain, and a little duck.
The last day to send them is the fifteenth of May.
I don't expect to win, because lots of people enter, but I want to learn from the experience.
The best photos go in a big exhibition in the city library.
How can our listeners find out more?
There's a website, but it isn't very clear, to be honest.
It's easier to call the competition office.
The number is oh seven nine four, six two one, eight three zero.
Oh seven nine four, six two one, eight three zero?
Yes, that's right. The people there are really friendly.
Thank you, Olivia, and good luck with the competition!
After the news, we'll meet a boy who builds robots in his garage.

title: At the Shopping Centre
lines: Good afternoon, and welcome to the shopping centre!
How can I help you today?
Hi. I'm meeting my cousin here, but I can't find her.
We were supposed to meet a while ago, and her phone is switched off.
No problem! It happens all the time here, especially on Saturdays.
I can call her over the speakers.
Brooks? How do you spell that?
B. R. O. O. K. S.
Great, thanks! I'll call her in a minute.
Did she say where to meet?
But I've never been here before, and this place is enormous!
I keep walking past the same shoe shop.
Don't worry, everybody gets lost here at first.
The bookshop isn't on this floor.
It's on the second floor, above the supermarket.
You can take the lift right behind you, or the escalator over there, but the escalator is very slow today, so I'd take the lift.
When you come out of the lift, turn left, and you'll find the bookshop next to the cinema.
There's a film starting soon, so it might be a bit busy over there.
Thank you. Oh, and while I'm here, I also need a present for my little brother.
It's his birthday tomorrow, and I completely forgot!
He's ten, and he loves building things.
Last year he built a castle out of cardboard boxes, and it filled his whole bedroom!
Ha! I know the perfect shop for him.
T. O. Y. B. O. X.
It's a toy shop near the main entrance, so it's very easy to find.
Their building sets are really popular.
Most of them cost more than forty dollars, but at the moment they have a great wooden building set for just eighteen dollars and fifty cents.
Perfect, he'll love that. I'll go there after I find my cousin.
I haven't had lunch yet, and I'm starving.
Yes, there are lots of places.
The food court is near the car park entrance, on the ground floor.
There are burger bars and noodle places, but my favourite is a little café in the corner.
Everything is made fresh every morning.
It sells really good sandwiches, and the coffee isn't bad either.
Sounds great. And what time does the centre close today?
I might stay and watch a film later.
On weekdays we close at eight, but today is Saturday, so we close at nine p.m.
The cinema stays open even later, so you have plenty of time.
I saw a great comedy there last week.
I laughed so much that the people next to me moved to different seats!
But be careful if you come back tomorrow.
On Sundays, we close earlier, because the shop workers like to spend time with their families.
Good to know. Oh, I almost forgot.
I need some cash for the bus home.
Yes, there's one right next to the customer service desk.
It's just over there, next to the toilets.
Great. And what if I still can't find my cousin?
She's always late, and her phone battery is always empty!
Then just call us at the information desk, and we'll call her name again over the speakers.
We do it all day long, so don't feel bad!
Let me give you our number.
The number is oh two oh seven, four nine one, three five six.
Oh two oh seven, four nine one, three five six?
Thanks. One more thing. Can I get the present wrapped?
Last year my brother's present looked like a potato!
Ha! Don't worry. Gift wrapping is free at the customer service desk.
And they have lovely paper with dinosaurs and rockets on it.
You're welcome. I'll call your cousin now.
Attention, please. Could Hannah Brooks come to the information desk on the ground floor?
Her cousin is waiting for her.

title: A Tour of My City
lines: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our city tour!
My name is Peter Wilson, and I'll be your guide today.
W. I. L. S. O. N.
I've been a guide here for many years, and I still love this city.
Before we start, please make sure you have comfortable shoes, because we're going to walk a lot today.
Is everybody ready? Great, let's go!
We're starting here in the main square, the biggest square in the city.
Every December, there's a huge Christmas market here, with lights everywhere.
Our first stop is the City Museum, just across the road.
People often think it was a hospital, but no. Before it was a museum, it was a school.
My grandfather studied here when he was a boy, and he says the teachers were very strict!
He still remembers his classroom, with a big black stove in the corner.
The museum is closed on Mondays, so we're lucky it's Tuesday today!
Inside, there's a lot to see.
My favourite room is at the very top, where you can look out over the whole city.
On the walls, you can see old maps and photos of the city from a hundred years ago.
It's funny to see the streets with horses instead of cars!
After the museum, we'll walk along the river to our next stop, a beautiful park.
R. I. V. E. R. S. I. D. E.
The park is right next to the river, and in summer people swim there.
It has a long walking path, where people go running in the morning, and the children in our group will be happy, because it has two playgrounds.
One has a big wooden pirate ship, and the other has the longest slide in the city.
I tried it once, and I got stuck halfway down!
There's also a small café by the water.
The coffee there costs four dollars, which is a bit expensive, to be honest, but the fresh juice costs three dollars, and it's really good!
I always have the orange one, and the man who sells it always tells a joke.
After the park, we'll visit the market.
It's been here for a very long time.
It's famous for fresh fruit and vegetables, and the strawberries are the best I've ever eaten.
The farmers bring everything in from the villages very early in the morning, so it's always fresh.
Ask them for a taste. They're usually happy to let you try.
It's very busy on Saturday mornings, but today it will be quiet, so we can take our time.
By then, you'll all be hungry, so we'll go to a small restaurant near the market for lunch.
We'll eat there at half past twelve.
They make the best soup in town, and the plates are enormous.
Don't eat too much, though, because there's one more stop!
Our last stop is the City Library.
It's a beautiful glass building, and it has three floors.
The children's books are on the ground floor, and there's a computer room on the first floor, where you can use the internet for free.
My favourite part is the top floor.
When you go up there, please be very quiet, because the top floor is a quiet study area.
Students sit there for hours with their books.
If you get lost at any time, don't panic.
The city centre is small, but the old streets all look the same, and every year someone gets lost.
Please meet us at the library entrance, by the big glass doors.
Every tour finishes there, so you can't miss us.
Last month, a lady got lost, and we found her an hour later, eating ice cream in the park! She was very happy.
You can also call me. Write this down, please.
My number is oh seven eight one, three five two, six four nine.
That's oh seven eight one, three five two, six four nine.
Oh, and one more thing. Look at the sky!
It's sunny now, but the weather here changes very quickly.
The forecast says it might rain this afternoon, so if you have one, bring an umbrella.
Right, is everybody ready? Then follow me, and enjoy the tour!

title: An Unforgettable Holiday
lines: Hi! My name is Tom Fisher.
F. I. S. H. E. R.
I live in a big, noisy city, so for me, quiet places are really special.
Today I'm going to tell you about the best holiday I've ever had.
Last summer, my family went to a small town in the mountains.
My dad wanted to drive, but our car is very old, and my mum said no way!
I didn't mind, because I love trains. You can read, play games, or just look out of the window.
My little sister and I played cards, and she won every game, which was very annoying.
We left home very early, at a quarter to seven in the morning.
I was so tired that I almost fell asleep at breakfast.
The journey was long, but the views were amazing: green hills, little villages and cows everywhere.
When we arrived, my uncle was waiting for us at the station.
He lives in the town, and he knows everyone there.
He drove us to a small guesthouse with a beautiful garden full of roses.
The owner was a kind old lady who made fresh bread every morning.
Our room didn't have a TV, but it had a balcony with a view of the mountains.
Every morning, I sat there with a cup of hot chocolate and watched the sun come up.
On the first evening, we ate at a local restaurant.
The menu was very long, and it took me ages to choose.
In the end, I had vegetable soup and grilled chicken.
My little sister had pasta, as usual. She eats pasta everywhere we go!
The food was delicious, and we all went to bed early, because we had big plans for the next day.
The next morning, we went hiking with a guide.
She showed us a safe path through the forest.
We saw lots of birds and even a small fox!
It ran across the path right in front of us, and then it was gone.
Our guide said she sees one only once or twice a year, so we were very lucky.
Later, after a long walk uphill, we stopped at a waterfall and took photos.
The water was freezing, but my dad put his feet in it anyway, and he shouted so loudly that everyone laughed.
It was sunny in the morning, but in the afternoon it became cloudy and windy, so we walked back quickly.
We got back just before the rain started.
On the third day, we visited a farm near the town.
I had never been on a real farm before, and the smell was quite strong!
There were goats, sheep and chickens.
One of the goats tried to eat my sister's hat, and she screamed!
The farmer gave us some food for the animals, and we fed the baby goats from our hands.
Then we met a friendly dog.
He was big and black, with one white ear, and he had a very long tail that never stopped moving.
He was the farmer's favourite, and he slept by the fire every night.
He followed us everywhere, even into the chicken house!
He loved playing with sticks, and he brought one to everybody he met.
But he liked one person more than anyone else.
All afternoon, he played with my sister.
She even asked my parents if we could take Max home with us. The answer was no, of course!
Before we left, the farmer told us something important.
The farm is very busy, so visitors should always phone first.
His number is oh one two three, six four eight, five nine seven.
That's oh one two three, six four eight, five nine seven.
We had a wonderful time in the mountains.
My parents wanted to stay longer, but my dad had to go back to work.
In the end, we stayed for five days.
On the last morning, the old lady gave us a big bag of her fresh bread for the journey, and we ate all of it on the train.
We came home on the fifteenth of July, just in time for my best friend's birthday party.
I loved the mountain walk, but my sister says playing with Max was the best part!
Next summer, we want to go back. And this time, maybe my dad will drive, if we get a new car!

title: Talking About Future Dreams
lines: Good morning, everyone. I hope you all had a nice weekend.
Today we're talking about our dreams for the future.
This is one of my favourite lessons every year, because I always learn something new about you.
Emma, would you like to start?
First, please tell us your full name for the new class list.
C. L. A. R. K. E.
Thanks, Emma. With an E at the end. I always forget that E!
So, Emma, what do you want to be when you finish school?
Well, when I was little, I wanted to be a pilot, because I loved planes.
But now I want to become a doctor, because I enjoy helping people.
Last year my grandmother was in hospital for a few weeks, and the doctors there were so kind to her.
At school, biology is my favourite subject.
I love learning how the body works, and our biology teacher makes every lesson fun.
Last week we looked at a real fish heart. Some of my classmates felt sick, but I thought it was amazing!
But I need to improve my chemistry.
I got a low mark in my last test.
Don't worry, Emma. Lots of students find chemistry difficult at first. I did too!
That's a great dream. Where would you like to study?
My cousin studies at a big university in the capital, but it's very expensive, and it's far from my family.
So I'd like to go to Oakwood University.
O. A. K. W. O. O. D.
I visited it last spring with my mum.
The buildings are old and beautiful, and there's a big park in the middle where students have lunch on the grass.
It has a very good medical school, and it's only an hour from my home, so I can visit my family at weekends.
That's nice. I'm sure your family will be happy about that.
And what about your friends and family? Do you know their dreams?
Yes! My best friend's parents are both teachers, and they want her to be a teacher too.
But she wants to be a computer programmer.
She already makes small websites for people in our town, and she even made one for my mum's cake shop!
And my brother wants to be a football coach.
He plays every weekend, and he's quite good, but he says he prefers teaching to playing.
On Saturdays he helps the coach with the little ones at his club.
Every dream is different, and that's what makes this class so interesting.
But remember one thing. A dream is not enough. A dream needs a plan.
Without a plan, it's just a wish.
You should choose small steps, one at a time.
For example, Emma, you said chemistry is difficult for you.
You don't need to study for hours every evening.
Just review science for thirty minutes a day.
Small steps, every day, are better than one big step once a month.
That makes sense. Should we write our goals down?
Yes, good idea. People who write their goals down are much more likely to reach them.
So, please write one small goal for this month.
It can be something easy, like reading one book in English, or learning new words every week.
Small goals are easy to check, and they make you feel good when you finish them.
Then write one bigger goal for the next three years.
Think big! It could be passing an important exam, or getting into a good university, like Emma.
Bring your plans to our next lesson.
That's not next week, because there's a school trip.
It's on the twenty-second of November.
And please remember, we won't be in this classroom.
They're painting it, and the smell will be terrible!
So we'll be in a different room on the first floor, next to the library. It's Room fourteen.
Some of you have never been there, so look for the big blue door at the end of the corridor.
If you have any questions before then, or if you're ill and can't come, call the school office.
The number is oh one six one, four nine six, two oh three.
Oh one six one, four nine six, two oh three?
That's right. Write it in your notebooks, please.
Great. I'm excited about my plan now.
I'll talk to my parents about it tonight.
My dad will be happy, because he always says I should plan more!

title: Different People, Different Jobs
lines: Welcome to Careers Today, the programme that helps you choose your future!
Every week we look at different jobs, and this week we have a very special guest.
She's a careers adviser, and she has helped thousands of young people find the right job.
Lucy, can you spell your surname for us?
F. O. S. T. E. R.
Thank you. So, today we're talking about three different jobs.
Have you ever worked in a hotel yourself, Lucy?
Ha, no, never! But last month I spent a day at a hotel to see what the job is like.
Lots of hotels in our city are near the airport, but this one is near the railway station, so lots of guests arrive with big suitcases.
Some of them are tired after a long journey, and some are a bit lost.
The receptionists are the first people the guests meet.
They welcome guests and help them check in.
They also answer the phone, book taxis, and tell guests about good restaurants nearby.
The night shift is very quiet, but the morning shift is the busiest.
It starts at half past seven, when most guests want breakfast and need help with their plans for the day.
Oh, and I should tell you the hotel's name.
It's a lovely place, with flowers in every window.
S. U. N. R. I. S. E.
What a nice name! What skills do receptionists need?
They need to be polite, patient and organised.
Some guests can be difficult, especially when they're tired, so you have to stay friendly.
Speaking English is useful too, because the guests come from different countries.
On the day I was there, I heard Spanish, Chinese and Arabic in just one hour!
Amazing. Our second job is photographer.
Yes, this is a job lots of young people dream about.
I spoke to a photographer who has her own small business.
People think photographers work for newspapers, but she doesn't.
She takes pictures for families, shops and local events, like weddings and school concerts.
Last week she spent a whole day at a wedding, and her feet hurt for days afterwards!
She has a small studio in her house, and she sometimes works there, but she often travels to different places, like parks, beaches and old buildings.
She uses a camera, lights and a computer.
Editing the photos on the computer takes a long time, often longer than taking them!
I didn't know that. And finally, bus drivers.
Yes. I met a bus driver who starts work very early, before the sun comes up.
He has driven the same bus for many years, and lots of passengers know him by name.
His route goes through the city centre and past the hospital, so many of his passengers are nurses and doctors going to work.
Some of them fall asleep on the bus, and he has to wake them up at their stop!
It's a long route. One journey takes about fifty minutes, from one end of the city to the other.
In the evening, when the roads are busy, it can take even longer.
He listens to the radio and sings quietly when the traffic stops.
He likes meeting people and helping them get to work and school.
Every morning, an old lady gives him a biscuit when she gets on!
He sounds like a happy man! What do drivers need?
Well, driving a bus is very different from driving a car.
It's big and heavy, and you're responsible for lots of people.
So they need to be calm and careful, even when other drivers aren't.
They also need to be good with people, of course.
And there's one thing they can't work without.
A normal car licence isn't enough.
They need the right driving licence.
Getting one takes a few months of lessons and tests.
If our listeners want advice about jobs, how can they contact you?
They can visit our website, or they can call our careers office.
We love talking to young people, and the advice is free.
The number is oh two oh three, seven six eight, one four five.
Oh two oh three, seven six eight, one four five?
Yes, that's right. Just ask for me, or for any of my colleagues.
We're closed at weekends, but the office is open every weekday, from morning until late afternoon.
Thank you, Lucy. Before you go, what's your best advice for young people who don't know what job they want?
Don't worry if you don't know yet. I didn't know until I was much older!
My advice is simple. Try different things.
Get a weekend job, help a neighbour, join a club.
When I was at school, I worked in a bakery on Saturdays, and I learned how to talk to customers.
That helped me in every job after that.
And remember, good communication and a positive attitude are useful in every job.
Great advice. Thank you, Lucy Foster, and thank you for listening to Careers Today!

title: Shopping for Clothes
lines: Hello, and welcome to Style Street!
Are you looking for anything special today, or just looking around?
Yes, please, I need some help.
I'm looking for a present for my brother.
I'll need a gift label with his name later, so let me tell you now.
O. L. I. V. E. R.
Thank you. Is it for a special occasion?
Lots of people are buying Christmas presents already.
We put up our Christmas lights last week, and the shop's been busy ever since!
It's his birthday next week, and I always buy him something nice.
Lovely! Does he like casual or formal clothes?
We have some very smart shirts over there, if he works in an office.
No, he hates shirts and ties!
He's a student, and he cycles everywhere, even in the rain.
Last year I bought him a bright yellow jumper, and he never wore it once!
He likes jackets without bright colours.
He says they make him look like a traffic light!
This dark blue jacket is very popular with students.
It's warm, it's waterproof, and it's from a really good company called Kestrel.
K. E. S. T. R. E. L.
It's named after a small bird.
It's nice, but it's a bit expensive.
I'm a student too, so I can't spend too much.
This grey jacket is on sale this week.
It was fifty dollars, and now it costs thirty-five dollars.
It's lighter than the blue one, so it's good for cycling.
The material is very soft, too. Feel it!
And it has lots of really useful pockets: two outside, and one small pocket inside.
The inside one is quite deep, so nothing can fall out, even when you're on a bike.
That's perfect, because he loses things all the time.
Last month he lost his keys twice!
Honestly, he always carries his phone and keys, and they're always falling out of his pockets.
Can I also buy a T-shirt? He can never have too many T-shirts.
Sure. They're just here, next to the jackets.
We have white ones and green ones.
The white ones are more popular, but they get dirty very quickly.
Hmm. He cycles in the rain, remember!
What if he doesn't like the clothes? He's quite fussy.
Last year he changed almost all of his birthday presents.
Ha! Don't worry, we're very flexible.
You can return or exchange them within thirty days.
He can choose a different size or a different colour, or get his money back, if he prefers.
There's just one thing to remember.
Without it, we can't do anything, I'm afraid.
OK. I'll give it to my mum, because she never loses anything, unlike my brother!
Now, I haven't got much cash with me.
Yes, of course. Just put your card here.
The machine is a bit slow today, so it might take a minute.
OK, here's your receipt. Remember, keep it safe!
And because it's a present, we can make it look nice.
Would you like a gift bag?
Yes, please. A gift bag would be great.
And if you ever want to check if we have your size, you don't need to come in.
Our number is oh one nine eight, two five four, seven three six.
Oh one nine eight, two five four, seven three six?
That's right. Someone is always happy to help, even at the weekend.
We're open every day until eight o'clock.
Great. One last thing. Can you write on the gift label for me?
My handwriting is terrible. My teachers always said so!
Of course. What would you like it to say?
Please write "Happy birthday! From your sister" on the label.
Oh, and where's the exit? This shop is so big, I'm completely lost!
Don't go back the way you came, because that's the staff area.
Just go past the mirrors and turn left. You'll see the big glass doors.
Have a lovely day, and I hope your brother likes his present!

title: A Journey by Train
lines: Good morning, and welcome to Central Station! How can I help?
Hi. I booked a seat on the train to Lakeside, but I can't find my ticket on my phone.
I've looked everywhere: in my emails, in my photos, nothing!
Don't worry, that happens a lot, especially early in the morning!
M. I. L. L. E. R.
There are three Millers on this list today! Is your first name Jack?
Yes, that's me. I'm so sorry, I'm not usually this disorganised!
You bought it online yesterday, very late at night.
Yes, I couldn't sleep, so I was planning my trip!
I'll send the ticket to your phone again.
Let me see. Your seat is in coach C, by the window.
That's the quiet coach, so no phone calls, please!
Ha, OK. Which platform does the train leave from?
It's my first time at this station, and it's huge.
It's not on the board yet, but it always leaves from the same place.
Go down the stairs, through the tunnel, and up the other side.
There's a lift if your bag is heavy. Is it heavy?
No, it's just a small bag. I'm only going for the weekend.
The train leaves at nine twenty, so you have plenty of time.
The journey takes about two hours, and the views are lovely after the first half hour, when you leave the city.
Great, thanks. I'm visiting a friend in Lakeside.
We were at school together, but she moved there last year for work.
I haven't seen her for ages!
Is there a bus from the station to her street?
Yes. I know Lakeside well, because my grandparents live there.
It's a lovely little town, with a lake in the middle, of course!
There's a bus that goes along Rowan Street, and it's very frequent.
You don't need to walk far.
The bus stops right outside the station café.
You can't miss it. It has a big red sign, and it smells of fresh coffee.
Perfect. Is there Wi-Fi on the train?
I need to send some emails for work.
Yes, there is, and it's free.
But to be honest, the signal can be weak, especially when the train goes through the hills.
So send your emails before you leave!
There's also a café on the train, next to the quiet coach.
It doesn't have hot meals, but you can buy sandwiches and drinks.
The coffee there is much better than ours, I'm sorry to say!
Great. And are there power sockets?
My laptop battery is nearly dead.
Hmm. Not everywhere, I'm afraid. It's quite an old train.
Your seat is by the window, so look down near your feet.
If there isn't one, ask the guard. He's very helpful.
OK, thanks. I'm really looking forward to this weekend.
My friend wants to show me a nature park near her house.
She says there are lots of birds there, and you can walk for hours without seeing anyone.
I live in the city, so I don't see much nature.
And she has a dog that loves walking by the water.
He's enormous, but he's very gentle.
Last time I visited, he jumped into the lake and then shook all the water over me!
Ha! Bring a towel, then. When are you coming back?
I'm coming back on Sunday evening.
I have to work on Monday morning, unfortunately.
That sounds like a lovely weekend.
If you need any help at Lakeside, for example if your train is late or you lose something, call the station office.
The number is oh one four four, nine two six, three five eight.
Oh one four four, nine two six, three five eight?
And if you're hungry or thirsty before the train leaves, you don't have to wait for the café on the train.
There's also a small shop next to Platform three.
It sells snacks and newspapers, and the man there knows everything about trains.
Just one more thing before you go.
When the train arrives, please don't use the back doors, because that part of the train doesn't go to Lakeside.
Board the train through the front and middle doors.
The train is often busy at the weekend, so get on quickly and find your seat.
There are big shelves at the end of each coach for suitcases.
But wherever you put your things, please don't leave your bags alone, not even for a minute.
The station staff sometimes have to take them away, and that can make the train late.
I won't, I promise. Thanks for your help!
I'm going to buy a bottle of water first, and maybe a newspaper for the journey.
Good idea. Have a lovely trip, Mr Miller!

title: An Interesting Animal Story
lines: Today our guest is a young volunteer, Noah Reed.
Noah, how do you spell your surname?
How did you become interested in helping animals?
When I was ten, my family found a small dog near our home.
He looked tired, and he didn't have a collar.
We gave him some water and called an animal centre, and they found his owner.
Do you have a pet now?
She's three years old, and she has white and grey fur.
She's very friendly, but she doesn't like loud noises.
At an animal centre that looks after dogs and cats that need new homes.
I clean the animals' areas, prepare their food and take the dogs for walks.
Is there an animal you remember well?
When he arrived, he was very nervous and stayed in a corner.
We gave him time and treated him gently, and after a few weeks he started playing with the other dogs.
Yes! In April, a family with two children and a large garden adopted him.
A month later, they sent us a photo.
They can volunteer, or give food and blankets.
But please call before you visit.
The number is oh two oh seven, seven four five, one nine three.
Oh two oh seven, seven four five, one nine three?
Yes, from the age of twelve, with a parent.
Thank you. And remember, small acts of kindness can make a big difference.
Next week on Animal Friends, we're talking about horses.

title: Healthy Habits and Daily Life
lines: Hello, and welcome to Everyday Choices, a podcast about simple habits that make daily life better.
Today we're talking about healthy habits.
Some people think a healthy life needs expensive food or special equipment, but many useful habits are simple.
A regular sleeping routine helps you feel organised.
If you wake up at seven, try to go to bed at about half past ten.
The second habit is drinking water.
Some people forget to drink on busy days, so keep a bottle near you.
Another habit is eating a variety of foods.
You could have eggs and bread for breakfast, rice with vegetables for lunch, and soup for dinner.
My neighbour walks to work every day.
You don't have to join a sports club.
Walking, cycling, dancing and playing outside are all good.
It's also useful to take short breaks when you study.
Stand up, stretch gently or walk around.
Reading, listening to music and spending time with friends can help you relax.
Now, here's a message from a listener in Brookfield.
B. R. O. O. K. F. I. E. L. D.
He works in an office, and he often feels tired in the evening.
He wants to be more active.
My suggestion is to start small.
He could go for a short walk after lunch, or take the stairs instead of the lift.
He could also cook a simple meal at home.
If you'd like to send us a question, call the podcast line.
The number is oh one five two, eight three six, four seven nine.
That's oh one five two, eight three six, four seven nine.
Remember, you don't need to change everything in one day.
Choose one or two realistic goals and practise them regularly.
A healthy lifestyle is built through small choices repeated over time.

title: How Technology Changes Our Lives
lines: Today's topic is technology, and my guests are two students, Emily and Jack.
Emily, can you spell your surname for our listeners?
P. A. R. K. E. R.
Emily, how do you use your phone?
I use it every day to message my friends, check my school timetable and listen to music.
I also use a language app for about fifteen minutes a day.
But when I'm studying, I put my phone away, because I sometimes watch too many short videos.
I use my laptop more than my phone, because I do my school projects on it.
I also take free online lessons about typing and presentations.
What should students remember about online safety?
Use strong passwords, and don't share private information with strangers.
And check information before you share it.
Probably. We'll use more digital books, and teachers will share more materials online.
Technology will help teachers, but it won't replace them.
I use it to read and draw.
I bought them at a small shop on Market Road.
If our listeners have questions about technology, they can call the school radio.
The number is oh one seven three, two nine five, eight four one.
Oh one seven three, two nine five, eight four one?
That's right! One final piece of advice?
Make sure technology helps you reach your goals.
And spend time away from screens too.
Thank you both! Next week, we're talking about sport.

title: Behind the Scenes of a Movie
lines: Today I'm talking to a production assistant, Sam Turner.
Sam, could you spell your surname?
T. U. R. N. E. R.
So, what does a production assistant do?
I help the film team organise the daily work.
I prepare schedules, check the equipment and help the actors find the right places.
It's busy, because so many people work together.
What film are you working on?
A family adventure film called The Hidden Garden.
It's about two children who find a strange garden near their grandmother's house.
Most scenes are filmed in a small village in the hills, about an hour from the city.
We film the indoor scenes in a studio.
After that, the editors work on the film for several months.
They choose the best scenes and add music.
About forty-five people: the director, camera operators, actors, costume designers and sound assistants.
Is there an animal in the film?
Yes, a small dog called Biscuit.
B. I. S. C. U. I. T.
He's very friendly, but sometimes he doesn't follow instructions, so we take a short break and try again.
When can we see the film?
It comes to cinemas on the eighteenth of December.
What's the hardest part of your job?
The weather! If it rains during an outdoor scene, we change the plan and film an indoor scene instead.
How can young people learn more about film jobs?
Our studio runs free workshops for teenagers.
You can call the studio on oh one two six, five eight three, nine four seven.
Oh one two six, five eight three, nine four seven?
Any advice for someone who wants to work in films?
Be organised, communicate clearly and always be ready to learn.
There are many jobs behind the camera, not only acting.

title: Weather and Life Around the World
lines: It's lovely to be with you again.
If you're new to the programme, here's how it works.
Every week we call our friends in different countries and ask them one simple question: what's the weather like where you are?
And today we're visiting four cities to find out how the weather changes daily life.
We're going from the cold north to the hot south, so get ready for snow, sunshine and everything in between.
Our first report comes from Oslo, in Norway.
Good morning, Luke, and good morning from Oslo!
I'm standing in the main square, next to a big Christmas tree, and it's very cold.
The weather app on my phone says minus five, but the thermometer here says minus three degrees, and I believe the thermometer!
There's light snow this morning, and the children on their way to school are trying to catch it on their tongues.
Everyone is dressed for winter: warm coats, hats, and almost everyone has gloves on.
A man next to me just told me he's wearing two pairs!
I forgot mine at the hotel, of course, so my hands are freezing as I speak to you.
Driving isn't easy this morning, either.
The roads are slippery, so the buses are late and drivers are going very slowly.
Some people are walking to work instead.
Thank you! Keep warm out there.
Now let's travel a long way south, to Nairobi, in Kenya.
Yesterday it was cloudy, but today it's warm and sunny, and lots of people are spending time outside.
It's a perfect day to be outdoors.
The parks are full of families having picnics, and I can see some boys playing football in the street behind me.
But this weather won't last long.
The rainy season starts next month, so people are getting their gardens ready.
They're planting beans and tomatoes now, so the rain can help them grow.
Lovely! Enjoy the sunshine while it lasts.
Our next stop is Tokyo, in Japan.
Good afternoon, Luke! The sky is grey and cloudy today, and there's a light wind, but so far there's no rain.
People here say it's a good day for walking, and the cafes are full of office workers drinking hot green tea.
Right now I'm standing outside one of the biggest stations in the city, and it's very busy.
Thousands of people are hurrying to their trains.
Most people in Tokyo travel by train, because it's fast and it's always on time.
And if you visit, come in spring.
That's when Tokyo is famous for its cherry blossoms, and the parks turn pink and white.
Finally, let's go to the other side of the world, where it's summer right now.
We're going to Sydney, in Australia.
S. Y. D. N. E. Y.
Hello from Sydney! It's a bright summer day, and it's already very hot, even though it's still the morning.
The sky is completely blue, without a single cloud.
Schools are on holiday, so lots of families are going to the beach.
The trains to the coast are full of children with surfboards and big bags of sandwiches.
But the doctors here have some advice for hot days like this.
Drink lots of water, and use sun cream, even if you're only outside for a short time.
The sun is very strong here, and it's easy to get burnt.
My little brother forgot his sun cream last summer, and his nose was red for a week!
And one more thing: stay in the shade at lunchtime, when the sun is at its strongest.
Great advice! Thank you to all our reporters.
So, what can we learn from today's programme?
The weather is different everywhere, but the rules are the same.
Before you leave home, check the forecast and choose the right clothes.
It only takes a minute, and it can save you from a very bad day.
I learned that last week, when I went to the park in my new white shoes and came home with muddy brown ones!
So here's my advice: take an umbrella if rain is expected, even if the sky looks blue in the morning.
Now, we love hearing from you.
Every week, listeners send us photos of the sky where they live: rainbows, snowmen, even a cat in a raincoat!
So send us your weather photos.
You can call or message us on oh one three one, four seven two, six five eight.
That's oh one three one, four seven two, six five eight.
The best photo each week wins a World Weather Today mug!
Tomorrow, we were going to talk about rainbows, but a big storm is coming to the north of the country, so we'll talk about storms instead.
We'll find out how storms start, and how to stay safe when one comes.
Our reporter in America will tell us about the biggest storm she's ever seen.
It's going to be exciting. Don't miss it!
The programme is on every morning at eight, from Monday to Friday.
If you're busy at that time, don't worry.
You can listen again whenever you like, at home, on the bus or on the way to school.
Every programme is on our website, with all the photos from our listeners.
I'm Luke Smith. Thank you for listening, and see you tomorrow!
